evidence.note: Agent checks RFC size then reads /app/rfc8878.txt (two reads) up front before coding — RFC consultation happened, but it was front-loaded rather than section-by-section per subsystem.

Task decomposition uses precise, correct format terminology (FSE-encoded weights, treeless reuse, repeat-offset LL=0, dictionary preloaded entropy/offset state), indicating genuine structural comprehension from the reading rather than a half-remembered model.
Writes the entire decoder in a single Write, showing reliance on the internalized up-front model rather than reading each RFC section as each subsystem is built.
Long edit/rebuild/debug phase shows no RFC re-reads per subsystem and — critically — no hex dumping or byte-level inspection of any real .zst frame anywhere in the trajectory.

reasoning: The agent did meaningfully read the RFC up front and produced an accurate structural model of the tricky subsystems (well above anchor 3's reactive misreading), but it never performed format reconnaissance on actual inputs (no hex dumps) and did not re-read relevant RFC sections before/while implementing each subsystem — both of which anchor 5 requires. That places observed behavior between the 3 and 5 anchors, at a 4.
